{{Short description|Traditional drink from Japan}}
[[File:Miki_Marumasa.JPG|right|thumb|''Miki'' from Marumasa (Miyako Island, Okinawa Prefecture)<!-- マルマサ（沖縄県宮古島）のミキ -->]]
'''''Miki''''' is a Japanese drink from [[Amami Ōshima|Amami Oshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a">{{Cite web |title=奄美大島のソウルドリンク「ミキ」ってどんな味？ |url=http://www.amamibussan.jp/info/food/amami-soul-drink-miki/ |access-date=2023-02-08 |website=奄美物産 公式ブログ |language=ja |archive-date=2023-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208231751/https://www.amamibussan.jp/info/food/amami-soul-drink-miki/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="琉球新報style-2022a">{{Cite web |title=「ミキ」を徹底研究してみた。→奥深さの沼にはまった。 「てみた。」１６ |url=https://ryukyushimpo.jp/style/article/entry-598076.html |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=琉球新報Style |date=22 October 2017 |language=ja |archive-date=2022-06-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220605132234/https://ryukyushimpo.jp/style/article/entry-598076.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Okinawa Prefecture]],<ref name="琉球新報style-2022a" /> areas known for health and longevity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hokama |first1=Tomiko |last2=Binns |first2=Colin |author-link2=Colin Binns |date=2008-10-01 |title=Declining longevity advantage and low birthweight in Okinawa |journal=Asia-Pacific Journal of Public Health |volume=20 Suppl |pages=95–101 |issn=1010-5395 |pmid=19533867}}</ref><ref name="琉球新報style-2022a" /> It is based on ''[[omiki]]'', a beverage used in [[Shinto]] rituals and festivals. ''Miki'' is made from fermented rice, sweet potatoes, and sugar and was traditionally made in every household on the island.<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" />  It is sold commercially as a [[soft drink]],<ref name="琉球新報style-2022a" /> with many specialized shops selling it,<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" /> and some grocery stores.<ref name="rice-milk-miki-|-okinawa-atoz-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Rice Milk Miki {{!}} Okinawa AtoZ |url=https://www.okistyle.com/a2z/?p=2417 |access-date=2023-02-09 |language=ja |archive-date=2023-02-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230209173005/https://www.okistyle.com/a2z/?p=2417 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== History ==
The origin of ''miki'' can be traced back to "''[[kuchikamizake]]''," an alcoholic beverage made by chewing rice or other grains and storing the saliva in a container.<ref name="soranews24-japan-news-2018a">{{Cite web |date=2018-09-27 |title=We've fallen in love with this quirky but yummy Okinawan rice "soul drink" |url=https://soranews24.com/2018/09/27/our-japanese-language-reporter-fell-in-love-with-a-yummy-yet-quirky-okinawan-rice-soul-drink/ |access-date=2023-02-09 |website=SoraNews24 -Japan News- |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-02-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230209173007/https://soranews24.com/2018/09/27/our-japanese-language-reporter-fell-in-love-with-a-yummy-yet-quirky-okinawan-rice-soul-drink/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="琉球新報style-2023a" />

It is related to ''[[amazake]]'' but contains many more ingredients such as barley and lactic acid.<ref name="soranews24-japan-news-2018a" />

This type of drink was commonly made and offered during the annual "umachi" event in villages and gateways. Miki is written as "{{Nihongo|[[omiki|divine sake]]|神酒}}" in [[kanji]] characters and has been recorded in historical accounts dating back to the 15th century.<ref name="琉球新報style-2023a">{{Cite web |title=「ミキ」を徹底研究してみた。→奥深さの沼にはまった。 「てみた。」１６ |url=https://ryukyushimpo.jp/style/article/entry-598076.html |access-date=2023-02-09 |website=琉球新報Style |date=22 October 2017 |language=ja |archive-date=2023-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208231756/https://ryukyushimpo.jp/style/article/entry-598076.html |url-status=live }}</ref> It was used in fertility festivals.<ref name="our-regional-cuisines-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Miki |url=https://local-cuisine.maff.go.jp/en/recipe/201/ |access-date=2023-02-09 |website=Our Regional Cuisines |language=en |archive-date=2023-02-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230209173001/https://local-cuisine.maff.go.jp/en/recipe/201/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

With modernization, the traditional method of mouth-chewing the ingredients was abandoned and commercialized miki is now made using rice, barley, and sugar. The addition of barley to rice is said to have originated in Itoman, where miki has been made at the gates during the umachi season. However, each region has developed its own sense of taste and variations in the miki-making process still exist.<ref name="琉球新報style-2023a" />

== Description ==
The main ingredients of miki are rice and sugar, and the drink is made by fermenting these ingredients together.<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" /> It contains [[sweet potatoes]] in Amami,<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" /> and barley in Okinawa.<ref name="rice-milk-miki-|-okinawa-atoz-2023a"/> 

The texture of miki is said to be yogurtlike.<ref name="rice-milk-miki-|-okinawa-atoz-2023a"/> It has a sweet taste similar to that of sweetened [[okayu|rice porridge]], or amazake. <ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mysterious delicious drink "Miki"-The topic "rice milk" was already in Okinawa !? [entabe.com] |url=https://entabe.com/news/gourmet/7339/rice-milk-miki-miyakojima |access-date=2023-02-09 |website=Entabe [Food and Restaurants News in Japan] |language=en}}</ref> It is not considered an alcoholic drink.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hisadome |first1=Hiromi |last2=Yoshizaki(obana) |first2=Yumiko |last3=Tamaki |first3=Hisanori |last4=Wada |first4=Koji |last5=Ito |first5=Kiyoshi |date=2010 |title=Analysis of miki (a traditional beverage in Amami Island) |url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jbrewsocjapan/105/3/105_3_167/_article/ |journal=Journal of the Brewing Society of Japan |volume=105 |issue=3 |pages=167–174 |doi=10.6013/jbrewsocjapan.105.167|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Methods of consumption ==
People typically drink miki chilled, but it can also be mixed with ice, juice, milk, [[Shōchū|''shochu'']], or wine. As it ferments, it becomes more sour, and some people prefer to drink it when it reaches a certain level of sourness. The shelf life of miki is around 10 days from production, so it is best to drink it as soon as possible. In addition to drinking, miki can also be used to make desserts such as dumplings with molasses or mixed with ''zenzai'' to make a Japanese-style dessert. It can also be added to fruit to make a yogurt-like dessert.<ref name="奄美物産-公式フロク-2023a" />

It is said to help sick people recover.<ref name="rice-milk-miki-|-okinawa-atoz-2023a" /><ref name="our-regional-cuisines-2023a" />
